references.context: Order theory and topology: inclusion-maximal member Z of the family of nonempty irreducible subsets of X, meaning no irreducible subset W⊆X properly contains Z; distinct from a largest irreducible subset.
references.reason: Maximality in an inclusion-ordered family is reusable independently of the irreducible-component definition, while the qualifying family here consists of irreducible subsets.
references.matching_note: Compare earlier inclusion-maximal connected subset candidate from connected components; do not conflate maximal with maximum cardinality or assume ambient openness.

references.disposition: Closure of an irreducible subset is irreducible, so inclusion-maximal irreducible subsets are closed.

references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.
references.matching_note: This is the ordinary quotient ring by an ideal. Distinct specific features of this occurrence (prime ideal, polynomial base ring, local ring, square-zero ideal or powers) remain in its mathematical source. It is not a general quotient module or a quotient topology.

references.context: Commutative algebra: given quotient map q:A→A/I of unital k-algebras and k-algebra map f:K→A/I, a lift is a k-algebra homomorphism g:K→A satisfying q∘g=f; existence need not imply uniqueness.
references.reason: The lifting diagram is independently reusable and can be checked apart from the requirement that lifts exist for all square-zero extensions, which defines formal smoothness.
references.matching_note: Compare missing.27872640483c961ad03d and missing.9b77bf68dde01674ecf2 lifting candidate family; preserve field-source K and base k.

references.disposition: These are structural claims accompanying the formal lifting definition, rather than extra conditions placed on an individual lift.

references.phrase: R-module structure on S via R→S
references.context: Algebra and module theory: restriction of scalars along unital ring homomorphism φ:R→S, giving the codomain S an R-module structure via r·s=φ(r)s; changing φ may change the action.
references.reason: Inducing a module structure by a specified ring homomorphism is independently reusable, not the same as merely knowing S is a ring or R-module without a chosen action.
references.matching_note: Same induced-scalar structure as used by flat ring maps; compare missing candidate identities in later global audit rather than silently merging contexts.

references.disposition: Transfers the module property to the codomain through restriction of scalars; not a property of S absent a specified ring map.
